chunks: From him, from a man, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu 'Abd-Darrah (peace be upon him); and it was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from al-'Ala' ibn Fudayl, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"The child (fetus) and the young one do not prevent inheritance (by being the sole heir) nor do they inherit, except what has given a sign of crying, and nothing that the womb concealed, even if it moved, except what the night and day differed upon (i.e., reached a specific age of gestation)."

key_terms.اللَّيْلُ وَالنَّهَارُ: The night and the day (referring to the duration of gestation)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a fetus to inherit inheritance in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential criteria for fetal inheritance, requiring both viability (signs of life like crying) and a minimum gestation period (distinguished by night and day) to prevent premature claims on the estate. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise biological markers to resolve disputes between the fetus and other heirs, ensuring equitable distribution of wealth.
